title: ZION: A Practical Confidential Virtual Machine Architecture on Commodity RISC-V Processors
problem: Existing RISC-V TEE architectures rely on process-level abstractions or custom hardware extensions, limiting compatibility and scalability for confidential virtual machine deployment on commodity RISC-V processors.
motivation: Cloud platforms (AWS, Azure, Google Cloud) increasingly require Confidential VMs to protect sensitive workloads, driving demand for VM-level TEE solutions on open ISAs like RISC-V.
method: ZION protects a virtual machine's memory by combining Physical Memory Protection (a built-in hardware feature controlling which code accesses which memory regions) with paging (dividing memory into chunks) for scalable isolation. It speeds up context switching between virtual CPUs with a faster code path that avoids redundant security checks. It also enables virtio devices to access memory securely using split page tables—where the same page appears at different privilege levels—without modifying the RISC-V processor.
key_novelty: ZION achieves confidential virtual machine execution on standard RISC-V processors without hardware modifications, using hierarchical memory isolation and split-page-table mechanisms.
contributions: Confidential VM architecture for commodity RISC-V without custom extensions
Secure vCPU mechanism optimizing context-switching performance
Hierarchical memory management combining PMP and paging for scalable isolation
Split-page-table design for secure virtio device memory sharing achieving <5% overhead
limitations: Not discussed; focus is on compatibility rather than absolute performance vs. custom TEE solutions.
primary_theme: Practical TEE on commodity RISC-V via memory virtualization
